input.rationale: Record the sourced startup-replay premise discovered while reading the recovery path, and execute a bounded four-case probe (two boundary controls, two triggers, two of them built from a real single-node cluster prefix) to test whether NewRaft() completes a legal committed-log replay.

investigations.question: When RestoreCommittedLogs replays committed entries inside NewRaft, can the replay fail to make progress because the FSM batch channel is produced into before its only consumer is started?
investigations.hypothesis: processLogs enqueues ceil(replayed/MaxAppendEntries) commitTuple batches into fsmMutateCh (capacity 128) during NewRaft, while runFSM, the only consumer of that channel, is started only after NewRaft returns; a replay of more than 128*MaxAppendEntries committed entries beyond the last snapshot should therefore block NewRaft permanently on the channel send, since shutdownCh can only be closed by Shutdown() on a *Raft that NewRaft never returns.
investigations.discriminator: Compare NewRaft return for replay sizes at and above the batch-capacity boundary, including a real cluster restart with and without a snapshot bounding the replay; a return in every case would refute the hypothesis.

knowledge.statement: NewRaft() calls restoreFromCommittedLogs() synchronously, which clamps the store's staged commit index to the last log index, sets the commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs flushes a commitTuple batch to r.fsmMutateCh every MaxAppendEntries entries and once more for the remainder, and the only goroutine that reads fsmMutateCh (runFSM) is started after NewRaft returns.
knowledge.conditions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true and a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; no snapshot restored at or above the staged commit index.

knowledge.statement: For the captured code, the startup replay can enqueue at most 128 batches because fsmMutateCh is created with capacity 128 and its send in processLogs selects only on that send and on r.shutdownCh; with DefaultConfig MaxAppendEntries=64 this allows at most 8192 committed entries beyond the last snapshot, so 8193 or more replayed entries have no enabled progress path (no consumer exists and shutdownCh has no closer).
knowledge.conditions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true, DefaultConfig values, restart with staged commit index exceeding last snapshot index by more than 8192.

scope.description: Four restart attempts with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled: a commit-tracking store seeded with 8192 committed command entries (exactly 128 batches), the same seeded store with 8193 entries (129 batches), and two restarts of the same-address retained state produced by a real single-node cluster that committed 8300 commands through the normal leader/commit/apply path, one after an explicit Snapshot() and one without a snapshot.
assumptions: The FSM batch channel capacity and MaxAppendEntries are constants of the captured code; the harness records both in every case event.
Each case builds its own stores and transport, so cases do not share state; the real-prefix cases reuse exactly the stores written by the producing raft.
NewRaft is invoked on its own goroutine and observed for a bounded window; a case that never returns is reported as returned=false rather than as a harness failure.
fsm_applied_sampled is a single observation at the end of the window, not a completion marker.
excluded: No assertions about commit safety, voting or membership; this probe addresses startup progress only.
Snapshots older than the staged commit index by fewer than 8193 entries are not varied; the with-snapshot control removes the replay entirely.

experiment.prefix: Per case the harness creates an InmemCommitTrackingStore (and InmemSnapshotStore, InmemTransport, assuranceFSM) and emits startup_case_<case> with the staged commit index, last log index, snapshot index and derived replay batch count. Seeded cases store LogCommand entries 1..N and stage commit index N. Real-prefix cases call BootstrapCluster for a single voter, start the producing raft with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, wait for leadership, apply 8300 commands through Apply futures on the leader, optionally call Snapshot(), then Shutdown(). The restart then calls NewRaft with a fresh Config (RestoreCommittedLogs=true), a fresh FSM and a fresh transport on the retained stores, bounded by the case timeout; startup_result_<case> records returned, elapsed_ms, error, sampled FSM apply count and the number of newly blocked processLogs/restoreFromCommittedLogs goroutines relative to a pre-case stack sample.
experiment.responsibility: The library, not the caller, owns the size and lifetime of its FSM dispatch channel: it chooses the batch size, creates fsmMutateCh, and decides the order in which NewRaft starts the FSM consumer. The documented RestoreCommittedLogs option promises to replay all known-committed logs on disk before completing NewRaft, so it must complete for a legal (store, commit index) state rather than block the caller that cannot yet shut it down.

comparisons.description: Exactly 128 replay batches (the channel capacity) must still let NewRaft complete.
A real-prefix restart whose snapshot bounds the replay must let NewRaft complete.
One entry past the 128-batch capacity must still let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.
A real cluster restart with 130 replay batches must still let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.

result.summary: Submitted sourced recovery-path records and a bounded four-case startup-replay experiment (two boundary controls, two real-cluster-prefix triggers) after local native feedback showed NewRaft blocks at 8193 committed entries. Interpretation citing the actual receipt is still to be written once the controller execution returns.
